role_in_parent: Translates cyclotomic divisibility information into the combinatorial accessibility condition needed on every coordinate stratum.
statement_nl: Let A,B,d be integers with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0. For j=1,...,d put w_j := B+j and let E := {A+1,...,A+d}. Assume that for every positive integer n one has #{ j in {1,...,d} : n divides w_j } <= #{ e in E : n divides e }. For each subset J of {1,...,d}, define Sigma(J) := { sum_{j in J} m_j w_j : each m_j is a nonnegative integer }. Then for every nonempty subset J of {1,...,d}, at least |J| elements of E lie in Sigma(J); equivalently, #(E intersect Sigma(J)) >= |J|.

domain_restrictions: w_j is defined only for indices j with 1 <= j <= d
E is defined as the set of integers A + 1 through A + d (so it has size d)
Sigma(J) uses coefficients m_j that are nonnegative integers for each j in J
the conclusion applies only to nonempty J
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers A,B,d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define w_j = B + j for j = 1,...,d and E = {A + 1,...,A + d}. Assume that for every positive integer n, the number of indices j in {1,...,d} with n dividing w_j is at most the number of elements e in E with n dividing e. Then for every nonempty subset J of {1,...,d}, the cardinality of the intersection of E with Sigma(J) is at least the cardinality of J.
quantifier_order: for all integers A,B,d such that A >= B and B >= 0 and d >= 0
for all integers j with 1 <= j <= d (definition of w_j)
for all positive integers n (hypothesis on divisibility counts)
for all subsets J of {1,...,d} (definition of Sigma(J))
for all subsets J of {1,...,d} with J nonempty (conclusion)

variables.name: d
variables.role: length parameter for indices j and the set E

variables.name: j
variables.role: index for defining w_j and for subsets J

variables.name: w_j
variables.role: value B + j used in divisibility counts and in Sigma(J)

variables.name: n
variables.role: divisibility test parameter in the hypothesis

variables.name: J
variables.role: index subset used to define Sigma(J)

variables.name: Sigma(J)
variables.role: all nonnegative integer linear combinations of {w_j : j in J}

variables.name: m_j
variables.role: coefficient in the representation of elements of Sigma(J), one coefficient for each j in J

witness_dependencies: To state membership of an element e in Sigma(J), there must exist a choice of nonnegative integers m_j (one for each j in J) such that e equals the sum over j in J of m_j times w_j; these coefficients depend on J and on the chosen e.
For the conclusion, for each nonempty J there are at least |J| distinct elements e in E such that e is in Sigma(J); the particular elements e and their representing coefficients depend on J.
